source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-03 api-core — scheduler push notifications silently dropped by legacy NotificationService stub)
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/notification.rs:348-356 — the `NotificationChannel::Push` arm of `NotificationService::send_to_user` is a no-op stub: it only emits `tracing::info!(... "Push notification (integration pending)")` and sends nothing. No device token lookup, no FCM/APNs call, no enqueue onto the `push_fanout_queue`. The Email arm (L322-347) and InApp arm (L357-381) do real work; only Push is a stub.

This NotificationService is the path the background scheduler uses. scheduler/votes.rs:95-97 calls `self.notification_service.notify_vote_started(...)`, and the notify_* builders all request the Push channel: notification.rs:488-491 (notify_vote_started -> InApp+Email+Push), :453-456 (notify_announcement_published -> InApp+Email+Push), :517 (notify_vote_ending_soon -> InApp+Push), :582 (notify_meter_reading_due -> InApp+Push), :634-637 (notify_payment_due -> InApp+Email+Push), :663 (notify_vote_reminder -> InApp+Push). Every one of these scheduler-driven notifications asks for Push and every one hits the no-op arm.

is_channel_enabled (notification.rs:239-243) first honours `pref.push_enabled`, so a resident who has explicitly enabled push for these event types still receives nothing on the Push channel; the channel loop then falls through and send_to_user logs success + calls record_sent (notification.rs:385-392), so the omission is masked as a successful send. Net effect: vote-started / vote-ending-soon / vote-reminder / announcement-published / meter-reading-due / payment-due push notifications generated by the scheduler are never delivered to devices.

A fully-implemented push path already exists but is a DIFFERENT subsystem (Epic 2B / 8A-3): NotificationPipeline wires `CombinedPushAdapter` (FCM+APNs) at notification_pipeline.rs:445-446, drained by `PushFanoutWorker` off the Redis `push_fanout_queue` (push_fanout.rs:25), with quiet_hours_drain.rs and notification_digest.rs built on top. The legacy NotificationService's InApp arm calls `granular_notification_repo.add_notification_to_group` directly (notification.rs:359-372) rather than through the pipeline's in-app adapter/pubsub, so persisting the in-app row does NOT enqueue a fanout job — i.e. the scheduler path does not get push via the modern worker either.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the no-op Push arm, the scheduler's use of NotificationService.notify_* with Push channels, and the pref.push_enabled gating are all confirmed by direct read. The one unverified link is whether some out-of-band mechanism re-delivers push off the persisted in-app row; the code read indicates it does not (legacy InApp write bypasses the pipeline adapter that would enqueue fanout), so this is a live non-delivery gap rather than defense-in-depth.

Fix (cloud-landable, backend-only): route the scheduler's notify_* calls through the existing NotificationPipeline / PushFanoutWorker instead of the legacy NotificationService, OR implement the Push arm of send_to_user to enqueue onto `push_fanout_queue` (reusing CombinedPushAdapter / the fanout job shape). Single-crate api-server edit; verifiable with `cargo test -p api-server` (add a test asserting a Push-channel notification produces a fanout job / delivery record rather than only a log line).

source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-10-03 api-core — bank-statement CSV import is non-atomic, leaves partial data on a mid-file parse error)
evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:49-107 — `process_statement_upload` performs multiple sequential writes against a bare `&mut PgConnection`: it first inserts the statement header (`create_bank_statement_rls`, L61-71), then loops over CSV rows inserting one line at a time (`create_bank_statement_line_rls`, L96-99). There is no transaction opened inside the service.

The per-row parse happens INSIDE the loop and early-returns: a bad row trips `result.map_err(... AppError::BadRequest("CSV parse error"))?` (L74-75) or the date parse `.map_err(... AppError::BadRequest("Invalid date format"))?` (L77-81). Because the connection is in autocommit mode, the statement header plus every line inserted before the failing row are already COMMITTED when the `?` returns the error. The matcher at L103 never runs.

The caller confirms autocommit: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/accounting/statements.rs:49-59 invokes `state.accounting_service.process_statement_upload(&mut rls, ...)` passing the pooled `RlsConnection` directly — it is NOT a `sqlx::Transaction` and no `BEGIN` is issued anywhere in the handler. On the returned BadRequest it maps to HTTP 400 (statements.rs:55-59) and returns, leaving the partial import persisted.

Impact: a manager uploading a bank statement whose Nth row is malformed (common with mixed bank-export CSV dialects — note the code already juggles `%Y-%m-%d` vs `%d.%m.%Y` at L77-78) gets a 400 'upload failed', but an orphaned BankStatement header plus its first N-1 lines remain in the DB, unmatched, with no cleanup path. Re-uploading the corrected file creates a DUPLICATE statement and duplicate lines, which then feed the payment matcher (duplicate PaymentMatch suggestions against the same invoices). This is a financial-data-integrity defect on a manager-only accounting path.

Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the non-transactional write sequence, the in-loop early-return, and the caller passing a non-transactional RlsConnection are all confirmed by direct read; not runtime-confirmed only because the exact partial-commit visibility depends on pool autocommit semantics (which is the sqlx default for a plain connection).

Fix (cloud-landable, backend-only): wrap the header+lines inserts in a single transaction (begin a `sqlx::Transaction` inside `process_statement_upload`, or validate/parse ALL rows up-front before any insert) so a parse error rolls back the whole import and no partial statement is persisted; run the matcher only after commit. Single-crate api-server edit; verifiable with `cargo test -p api-server` (add a test that uploads a CSV with a malformed trailing row and asserts zero statements/lines persisted).
